Core rule implementations (require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation): - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - ESLint RuleModule with meta, schema, messages, and create(context). - Annotated with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md. - Uses shared helpers from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode. - Uses buildVisitors from src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts to handle function-like AST nodes. - meta.messages.missingStory clearly instructs adding an explicit @story annotation and gives an example story file path. - meta.schema exposes options: - scope: array of strings, enum DEFAULT_SCOPE. - exportPriority: string, enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES.
- src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - ESLint RuleModule enforcing @req annotations on functions. - Annotated with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and multiple @req entries mapping to this story’s requirements. - Imports and uses DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, and shouldProcessNode from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts. - Uses checkReqAnnotation from src/utils/annotation-checker.ts to perform detection and reporting. - meta.docs.description: "Require @req annotations on function-like exports (declarations, expressions, and methods, excluding arrow functions)". - meta.messages.missingReq: actionable message that names the function, tells user to add @req, and gives an example format ("@req REQ-EXAMPLE"). - meta.schema options mirror require-story-annotation: scope (enum DEFAULT_SCOPE), exportPriority (enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES).
Shared detection, scope, and export-priority behavior (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - DEFAULT_SCOPE: ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"]. This matches the story’s required constructs and excludes arrow functions by default. - EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES: ["all", "exported", "non-exported"].
- src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - isExportedNode(node): walks the parent chain for ExportNamedDeclaration or ExportDefaultDeclaration to determine export status. - shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority): - Returns false if node.type is not in scope. - Applies exportPriority semantics: - "all": process regardless of export status. - "exported": process only if isExportedNode(node) is true. - "non-exported": process only if isExportedNode(node) is false. - hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node): unified detection strategy composed of: - jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node) using getJSDocComment. - commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node) via sourceCode.getCommentsBefore. - leadingCommentsHasStory(node) using node.leadingComments. - linesBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node, LOOKBACK_LINES). - parentChainHasStory(sourceCode, node). - fallbackTextBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node). - resolveTargetNode(sourceCode, node): returns the node to which @story JSDoc should be attached (handles TSMethodSignature, FunctionExpression, ArrowFunctionExpression, VariableDeclarator, ExportNamedDeclaration, ExpressionStatement, etc.). - extractName(node): robustly extracts a readable name from id, key, name, or literal key values; returns "(anonymous)" if not found. - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?): - Uses extractName to get functionName. - Calls hasStoryAnnotation; exits early if @story already present. - Chooses a resolvedTarget for fixes via resolveTargetNode. - Reports via context.report with: - node: identifier/key when available for precise error location. - messageId: "missingStory". - data: { name, functionName: name }. - fix + suggest entries that call createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget), inserting the ANNOTATION. - reportMethod(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?): similar to reportMissing but specialized for method-like nodes, uses createMethodFix and ensures error anchoring on the method name. - Explicit exports include: DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode, reportMissing, reportMethod, and helper detection functions.
- src/utils/annotation-checker.ts - getJsdocComment(sourceCode, node): wraps sourceCode.getJSDocComment. - getLeadingComments(node): accesses node.leadingComments safely. - getCommentsBefore(sourceCode, node): wraps sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) || []. - combineComments(leading, before): merges comment arrays. - commentContainsReq(c): checks if comment.value contains "@req". - linesBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node): - Uses sourceCode.lines and node.loc.start.line. - Scans up to LOOKBACK_LINES lines before the node for "@req". - Guards for missing lines or loc. - parentChainHasReq(sourceCode, node): - Walks up parent chain, using getCommentsBefore and leadingComments to look for @req. - fallbackTextBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node): - Uses sourceCode.getText() and node.range when available. - Looks back FALLBACK_WINDOW characters for "@req". - Wrapped in try/catch to handle malformed ranges or source. - hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context?, node?): - Uses advanced heuristics when sourceCode + node available: linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq. - Falls back to checking jsdoc.value and comments for "@req". - Wrapped in try/catch to prevent errors from breaking lint runs. - getFixTargetNode(node): parallels resolveTargetNode, selecting the appropriate outer AST container (MethodDefinition, VariableDeclarator, ExpressionStatement) for fix insertion. - createMissingReqFix(node): returns a named fixer that inserts "/** @req */\n" before the chosen target node. - reportMissing(context, node, enableFix = true): - Uses getNodeName and parent fallback to get a human-readable name, defaulting to "(anonymous)". - Chooses a nameNode (id, key, or node) for precise error location. - Constructs context.report options with messageId "missingReq" and data { name, functionName: name }. - Conditionally attaches fix: createMissingReqFix(node) when enableFix is true. - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options?): - Obtains sourceCode from context. - Fetches jsdoc, leading comments, commentsBefore, and combines them. - Calls hasReqAnnotation; if false, calls reportMissing(context, node, enableFix). - Independent of scope/exportPriority by design; scope is enforced in the calling rule via shouldProcessNode.
Visitor wiring for function-like constructs (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT, arrow-exclusion semantics): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts - buildFunctionDeclarationVisitor(context, sourceCode, options): - Returns { FunctionDeclaration: handleFunctionDeclaration }. - handleFunctionDeclaration: - Checks options.shouldProcessNode(node); returns early if false. - Uses resolveTargetNode(sourceCode, node) and helperReportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, target). - buildFunctionExpressionVisitor(...): - Returns { FunctionExpression: handleFunctionExpression }. - handleFunctionExpression: - Skips when node.parent.type === "MethodDefinition". - Otherwise uses resolveTargetNode + helperReportMissing. - buildArrowFunctionVisitor(...): - Returns { ArrowFunctionExpression: handleArrowFunctionExpression }. - handleArrowFunctionExpression: - Calls options.shouldProcessNode(node); since DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include "ArrowFunctionExpression", arrows are excluded by default. - If ever included in scope in future configuration, they would be processed. - buildTSDeclareFunctionVisitor(...): - Returns { TSDeclareFunction: handleTSDeclareFunction }. - handleTSDeclareFunction uses helperReportMissing. - buildTSMethodSignatureVisitor(...): - Returns { TSMethodSignature: handleTSMethodSignature }. - Uses resolveTargetNode + helperReportMissing. - buildMethodDefinitionVisitor(...): - Returns { MethodDefinition: handleMethodDefinition }. - Uses helperReportMethod to report + fix. - buildVisitors(context, sourceCode, options): merges all of the above into a single RuleListener used by require-story-annotation. - Together with DEFAULT_SCOPE and shouldProcessNode, - Both require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation enforce annotations on FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - ArrowFunctionExpression is wired but excluded from default scope, satisfying "Arrow functions are excluded by default from traceability requirements" while still allowing future configurability.
JSDoc parsing & error handling (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING and Error Handling acceptance criterion): - @story/@req extraction: - For @story: hasStoryAnnotation uses jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, line lookback, parent chain, and fallback text scanning. - For @req: hasReqAnnotation uses equivalent heuristics but looks for "@req". - Error handling: - hasStoryAnnotation, reportMissing, and reportMethod (story helpers) are wrapped in try/catch, swallowing unexpected parsing or IO errors and preventing ESLint failures. - hasReqAnnotation and fallbackTextBeforeHasReq use try/catch to guard against malformed loc/range/sourceCode state. - All detection helpers guard against undefined or incorrectly typed values (e.g., typeof sourceCode.getJSDocComment === "function"). - This matches "Gracefully handles malformed JSDoc comments and edge cases" in acceptance criteria.
Scope configuration and exportPriority (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - Shared options and semantics: - require-story-annotation.meta.schema[0].properties: - scope: array of strings, items from DEFAULT_SCOPE, uniqueItems true. - exportPriority: string, enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - require-req-annotation.meta.schema[0].properties: - scope: array, items.enum DEFAULT_SCOPE, uniqueItems true. - exportPriority: enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - Implementation: - Both rules read first options object and derive: - scope: use DEFAULT_SCOPE when undefined/empty; or provided array. - exportPriority: default to "all" when omitted. - Both rules use shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) from require-story-helpers to determine if a given node should be checked. - Tests demonstrating consistent scope/exportPriority behavior: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - "require-story-annotation with exportPriority option" block: - Valid: local (non-exported) function missing @story is allowed when exportPriority = "exported". - Valid: exportedAnnotated() with @story under exportPriority = "exported". - Valid: exported arrow function without @story under exportPriority = "exported" (arrows remain excluded). - Invalid: exportedMissing() without @story under exportPriority = "exported"; auto-fix + suggestion checked. - "require-story-annotation with scope option" block: - Valid: arrow function ignored when scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"]. - Invalid: FunctionDeclaration onlyDecl() without @story is reported when scope only includes FunctionDeclaration. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - Valid cases cover: - scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"] ignoring FunctionExpression. - exportPriority: "exported" ignoring non-exported, requiring exported functions. - exportPriority: "non-exported" ignoring exported, requiring non-exported functions and methods. - Invalid cases cover: - FunctionDeclaration reported when scope includes it explicitly. - exportPriority "exported" or "non-exported" for functions, function expressions, and methods, verifying consistency with require-story-annotation.

traceability.notes:
The implementation of `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` fully satisfies the story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS. Both rules enforce their respective annotations on the same set of function-like constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), with arrow functions excluded by default via shared DEFAULT_SCOPE and shouldProcessNode. A shared detection and configuration layer (scope and exportPriority) ensures both rules behave consistently, as required by REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY.
JSDoc and comment parsing for @story and @req is robust and shared in concept: each uses multiple heuristics (JSDoc, leading comments, commentsBefore, line lookback, parent-chain scanning, and fallback text windows) with defensive coding and try/catch blocks, fulfilling REQ-JSDOC-PARSING and the acceptance criterion for graceful handling of malformed JSDoc and edge cases.
Error messages are clear and actionable, include function/method names, and are reported at the appropriate identifier/key nodes, satisfying REQ-ERROR-LOCATION and the user-experience acceptance criteria. TypeScript constructs TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature are supported in both detection and reporting layers, and are thoroughly tested using @typescript-eslint/parser, meeting REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT and the Integration criterion.
Comprehensive RuleTester suites for both rules validate correct behavior across JS and TS, various function forms, options for scope and exportPriority, and the presence/absence of annotations. Documentation for both rules is present, aligned with the story, and details configuration options and examples. The Jest test suite, which includes these rule tests, runs successfully via `npm test`, providing concrete evidence that the implementation matches the specification.
Given this evidence, the story’s acceptance criteria and requirements are fully implemented and verified, so the status is PASSED.
